meta.description: Golden accuracy dataset. Each workload is priced by PolyCost and compared, per provider, against the real AWS/Azure/GCP Pricing Calculator monthly total within a tolerance. This is the proof that 'PolyCost's numbers equal a manual provider calculation'.
howToCapture: 1. For each workload below, open the AWS, Azure, and GCP public pricing calculators.
2. Configure the equivalent resources (same region, on-demand, same size/quantity).
3. Read the calculator's monthly total and put it in expected.<provider>.calculatorMonthlyUsd.
4. Set capturedAt to the date you captured it and keep source specific (SKU + region).
5. Leave calculatorMonthlyUsd null to run that provider in report-only (capture) mode.
6. Run: npm run pricing:accuracy:golden  (against a running stack; live mode for real numbers).
meta.toleranceNote: tolerancePercent is the allowed absolute deviation between PolyCost's monthly total and the calculator total before the row is marked FAIL.

workloads.description: 2 x general-purpose 2 vCPU / 8 GB Linux on-demand instances, no storage/db/network. The most predictable reference: monthly = hourlyRate x 2 x 730.
